info.bio:
The Undisputed Truth was a 1970s Motown recording act, assembled by record producer Norman Whitfield as a means for being able to experiment with his psychedelic soul production techniques. Joe Harris served as main lead singer, with Billie Rae Calvin and Brenda Joyce, formerly of The Delicates, on additional leads and background vocals.

History
The group's music and unusual costuming (large Afros and white makeup) typified the then-popular trend of "psychedelic soul".

scenes.name: Motown, Norman Whitfield y la psicodelia soul
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: El imperio de Berry Gordy fue un fenómeno de capitalismo negro, pero en los setenta solo sobrevivieron los artistas que escribían su material (Stevie Wonder, Marvin Gaye, Smokey Robinson, Michael Jackson). Norman Whitfield, que pasó de chupatintas a productor, le dio un filo más áspero («I Heard It Through the Grapevine» de Gladys Knight) y, mientras Sly arrasaba en 1968, cambió el sonido de los Temptations: temas largos con guitarras rockeras, efectos espaciales, drogas («Cloud Nine», «Psychedelic Shack», «Ball of Confusion») y orgullo negro, ropa a lo Hendrix y, al final, «Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone» (1972), soul con mensaje. La huella de P-Funk era clara (Eddie Hazel y Billy Nelson tocan en «Shakey Ground»); Whitfield convirtió a los Undisputed Truth en una banda de black rock pintada de plata. Los músicos de sesión, los Funk Brothers, trabajaban en la sombra: el bajista James Jamerson, que sacaba líneas de cómo hablaba o caminaba la gente, influyó a todos. Cuando Motown se mudó a Los Ángeles, la banda se quedó en Detroit y la magia se perdió.

scenes.name: Monster funk: la tercera dinastía
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: El fantasma del disco solo intensificó el funk de baile de los verdaderos funkers: la Edad de Oro del baile y la cima del movimiento. La influencia de P-Funk llenó las bandas de capas, viajes espaciales y personajes («Captain Quick Draw», «Big Chief Funkum», «Jupiter», «Wonder Worm» de Captain Sky, «Galaxy» de War, «Long Stroke» de ADC Band). Brick, quinteto de Atlanta, inventó con «Dazz» (1976) el «disco-jazz», con el bajo de Ray Ransom y la flauta funky de Jimmy Brown; nunca fue banda de disco. El Medio Oeste fue el semillero: Slave, de Dayton (Steve Washington, sobrino de un Ohio Player, el bajo de Mark Adams, la guitarra de Drac Hicks), con «Slide» y luego la voz de Steve Arrington; Sun («Radiation Level»); Lakeside, empaquetados por SOLAR con un disfraz por disco («It’s All the Way Live», «Fantastic Voyage»). De Vallejo, Con Funk Shun («Ffun»). «Con el funk no hay reglas», decía Washington.

podcast.title: Shared Appearances on American Bandstand and Soul Train (1976-1977)
podcast.body: The Undisputed Truth performed on both American Bandstand and Soul Train during 1976 and 1977. This overlapping presence of artists indicated that there was ample room for both television music shows to thrive concurrently. "the undispeed of truth is on both shows."

podcast.title: Minor Motown Act
podcast.body: Little Joe Harris, who had been taught by Abraham Silver alongside Martha Reeves and future Motown stars, later became the lead singer for The Undisputed Truth, described as a minor Motown act. "Little Joe Harris, who would later become lead singer of the Minor Motown Act, The Undisputed Truth."

podcast.title: Motown's Evolving Sound
podcast.body: In 1971, "Smiling Faces Sometimes" signaled a departure for Motown from its established formula, adopting a distinctively funkier sound. This shift occurred at a time when Motown, like James Brown, faced criticism from African Americans for its perceived lack of political engagement, as Berry Gordy had historically been cautious about political statements in his music until the early 1970s. "It's 1971 and Motown is finally starting to get out of that formula that they had that was so popular in particular with white people that's a very different funky or sound for Motown."
